name: amount-pad
title: Amount Pad
description: A send-money keypad. Digits spring into a large amount that shrinks to fit, with quick presets, a balance line and a cap that refuses amounts past the limit.
use: A payment step wants a big, thumb-friendly keypad instead of a text field, with quick preset amounts.
avoid: It is built for one-off transfers under a fixed cap; editing a saved amount or entering long figures is cramped.
a11y: Keyboard entry works and the amount is announced; Send is only aria-disabled, so it stays focusable and clickable while empty. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A tall dark rounded card. A small orange initials badge and a Send to Maya Chen @maya line sit at the top over a huge amount, a balance line and three preset pills. Below, a three-by-four keypad of digits, a dot and a backspace sits over a full-width Send button.
behaves: Tapping a key springs the digit into the amount while the number shrinks to stay on one line and commas slot in. Send wakes once a value exists, turns green with a tick after sending, then clears; typing past the cap shakes the number and shows a limit message.
customise: Recipient, currency, cap, balance, presets and an onSend callback are props; colours, key order and animation springs are fixed in the source.
weight: light: About a dozen buttons and a few spring animations; nothing runs when idle.
demo: Sending to Maya Chen @maya, balance $3,204.18, presets $20, $50 and $100.
issues: Send is only aria-disabled, so it looks inert but still takes clicks when empty.
polishWhy: Large self-fitting amount, clear keypad rhythm and a satisfying send-to-green state.
